dedupe_keys.name: two centuries of systemic bank runs database bank run chronology and national deposits 1800 2024 jamilov konig muller and saidi

description: This database records bank runs in 192 countries from 1800 to 2024, combining a narrative chronology of 405 run episodes drawn from 667 sources with a harmonised dataset of national banking sector deposits used to flag significant deposit contractions. Runs that coincide with country-level deposit outflows are classed as systemic; the authors find these are followed by output losses of about 9% over five years, even when panic, not weak fundamentals drives them, and that deposit insurance and a central bank lower the chance of runs turning systemic. It was built by Rustam Jamilov, Tobias König, Karsten Müller and Farzad Saidi and published as CEPR Discussion Paper 19382 in 2025, with a paper version dated July 2026. Coverage is global. Both datasets can be downloaded free from the project website, which also compares the chronology with four existing crisis lists; no licence is stated. Caveats: narrative identification depends on the historical sources consulted, and the paper is still being revised. For simulation it gives base rates and macroeconomic costs of depositor panics, useful for calibrating contagion and liquidity stress scenarios in which a bank run cuts credit to infrastructure operators and firms. It is related to the BIS survey case study on panic-driven bank runs after the SVB collapse in this catalogue.
